correctness.rationale: The equation for centrally symmetric two-cycles reduces exactly to a cubic in y=x^n. Its discriminant and sign pattern give exactly two positive roots for n>=18. The source critical-value identity places them on opposite sides of the unique positive free critical point. The inner multiplier is less than -1 from the sign of the cubic derivative. For the outer multiplier, an exact resultant excludes multiplier +1 throughout the continuous real-parameter branch n>=18, and an exact n=18 rational bracket fixes the sign as greater than +1. Oddness then squares these derivatives to period-two multipliers greater than 1. The packaged symbolic verifier replays the nontrivial algebra exactly.

value.rationale: The focal paper explicitly leaves convergence for even n>=18 open and notes that attracting or parabolic periodic domains are not excluded. The symmetry-reduced real critical lines are the canonical one-dimensional locus used by the paper to control the origin basin and to track free critical orbits. Proving that both centrally symmetric period-two cycles on every such line are repelling removes the most immediate period-two attractor/parabolic candidates uniformly in the unresolved regime. The exact count also identifies the complete symmetry-forced pair rather than an arbitrary numerical slice. The result is narrow but structurally tied to the paper’s open dynamical question.
